newsitem.title: USA: Quality Systems falls after EPS view cut.
newsitem.headline: Quality Systems falls after EPS view cut.

text.p: Shares in Quality Systems Inc led the Nasdaq market's percent-losers early Wednesday on selling motivated by a cut in revenue and earnings estimates by Pacific Growth Equities, traders said.
The shares fell to a new year-low 7-3/8 from 10-3/4 before trimming the loss to trade at 8-1/4, a loss of almost 24 percent.

Fred Toney, the Pacific Growth analyst who tracks the stock, said he revised the forecast because the integration of sales from the company's Clinitec acquisition is taking longer than originally expected.
Also, Clinitec's market has a longer selling cycle, further delaying gains from the acquisition.
No one was immediately available at Quality to comment.

For the 1997 fiscal year ending in March, Toney said he now expects the company to post $24 million in revenues, cut from $28 million and the earnings forecast is now $0.56 per share, down from $0.65 per share.
For fiscal 1998, the analyst now expects revenues of $38 million, down from $42.5 million, and earnings of $0.90 per share from $1.04.
He still rates the stock a buy, and said order backlog remains strong.
Quality Systems develops health care information systems for medical and dental group practices.
In the fiscal year ended last March, the company reported revenues of $16.7 million and earned $0.48 per share, up from $12 million and $0.21 per share in fiscal 1995.
